doc.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Playing with everybody in the New York studios
summary: Being available in the studios let him work with nearly everyone, from Gerry Mulligan to Phil Woods, except a few like Miles Davis.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Good words. The list of people you’ve played with since then is most impressive: Gerry Mulligan you played with, Sebesky and Phil Woods.

Yup, yup. Well being in New York and being in the studios, and being available, really available, I’ve had a chance to work with everybody. I mean just about everybody. I mean Miles Davis was one of the few I didn’t work with, I could name a small list of people who I never got a chance to play with. But in one capacity or another, either in the © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-
studios or a one-nighter, subbing for somebody, steadily, working steadily, or recording, I’ve really had a chance to work with a lot of people and hear a lot of music.
